high.title: Jensen Huang: Chip Industry Won't Face Downturn Anytime Soon — AI Godfather Says "This Time Is Different"
high.summary: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang pushed back against growing "AI bubble" narratives in a media interview, asserting that the current semiconductor boom is structurally different from previous cycles. His core argument: demand is not seasonal or cyclical, but driven by a fundamental transformation in computing infrastructure across all industries. Huang projected the global semiconductor industry must scale 5–10x over the next decade to meet AI infrastructure requirements, fueled by hyperscalers committing hundreds of billions annually in capex. Institutional investors noted Huang's public reassurance helped stabilize market sentiment during a period of volatility. For Taiwan-focused fund managers, the implications are direct and significant: TSMC (2330), ASE Technology (3711), Nanya Tech (2408), and Winbond (2344) are all cited as key beneficiaries of continued AI-driven chip demand. The commentary is particularly relevant following TSMC's recent post-earnings dip, which Nomura separately characterized as a consolidation rather than a fundamental deterioration. Huang's confidence signal may support a re-rating of AI-exposed Taiwan names in the near term.

high.title: Apple Earnings Expected to Beat Estimates — Cook's Final Meeting to Benefit Taiwan Supply Chain
high.summary: Apple is scheduled to report its fiscal Q3 results after the U.S. close on July 30 (Taiwan time: July 31 early morning), with consensus expecting revenue of approximately USD 108.6 billion and diluted EPS of USD 1.89 — likely surpassing the company's own guidance range of USD 107–110 billion with ~48% gross margins. This earnings release carries additional weight as it will be CEO Tim Cook's final conference call before his September retirement, with markets watching for signals from incoming CEO John Ternus. Critically for Taiwan investors, a strong Apple beat and optimistic forward guidance would directly benefit key supply chain names: TSMC (2330) for advanced node chips, Hon Hai/Foxconn (2317) for assembly, ASE (3711) for packaging, and Largan (3008) for optics. The anticipated launch of iPhone 18 and Apple's first foldable iPhone in H2 are additional demand catalysts. A positive outcome could re-energize the broader Taiwan tech supply chain and provide near-term price support across these names.

high.title: Five Key Industries Set to Benefit from US Tariff Advantages — 10% Non-Stacked Rate Unlocks Order Diversion Opportunities
high.summary:
Taiwan's preferential 10% non-stacked tariff treatment from the US is creating meaningful competitive advantages for five key export industries: bicycles, machine tools & machinery, hand tools & plumbing hardware, petrochemicals & textiles, and medical devices. Compared to China and most other Asian competitors still facing elevated US tariffs, Taiwan manufacturers are now better positioned to capture order diversion and restocking demand from American buyers.

The machinery sector is already seeing early positive signals. Cheng Tai Group Chairman Yang De-hua, following a recent US client visit, reported that American distributors responded enthusiastically to Taiwan's tariff status and are actively placing advance orders — with his group expecting 35–40% US revenue growth this year. He noted that Taiwan's tool machine exports previously faced higher US tariffs than Japan and Korea, but this dynamic has now reversed. The Taiwan Machine Tool Industry Association confirmed that major listed players including Cheng Tai (1583), Asia Pacific Elite Corp (1530), Tong Tai (4526), Kao Fong (4510), Hiwin (2049), and Taiwan Takisawa (4583) are reporting order growth of 15–40% versus early 2026.

high.title: Microsoft to Rent Computing Power, Further Boosting Infrastructure Demand — Hon Hai, Quanta Among Key Beneficiaries
high.summary: According to Business Insider, Microsoft — ahead of its Q4 FY2026 earnings release on July 29 — is reportedly in talks to rent computing capacity from Amazon AWS and Google due to insufficient in-house AI capacity. Despite a record capital expenditure budget of USD 190 billion for 2026 (predominantly allocated to AI infrastructure), demand growth is outpacing build-out, forcing Microsoft to seek external capacity to ensure continuity of AI services including Microsoft 365 Copilot, GitHub Copilot, and Microsoft Copilot. This dynamic signals that AI infrastructure demand remains structurally robust, defying recent bubble concerns. For Taiwan's AI server supply chain, the implications are strongly positive: Hon Hai (2317), Quanta, Wistron, Wiwynn, and Inventec stand to capture incremental server orders as hyperscalers accelerate infrastructure expansion. Market focus will also be on whether Microsoft guides for higher capex in FY2027 during its earnings call. This represents a near-term positive catalyst for Taiwan's AI hardware names and reinforces the thesis that capex cycles from U.S. cloud majors remain intact.

high.title: NVIDIA Backs OpenAI's Super Data Center — Hon Hai Shipments Poised for Surge
high.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that NVIDIA is set to provide USD 250 billion in financing guarantees to enable OpenAI to lease a massive 10GW data center being developed by SoftBank in southern Ohio, as part of what would be the largest AI data center project in history, with total investment potentially exceeding USD 500 billion (approximately NTD 16.2 trillion). Industry sources indicate that Hon Hai (2317), as a key strategic partner to both OpenAI and SoftBank, is expected to play a central role supplying AI servers and data center hardware, with shipments potentially seeing an explosive increase. The structure involves NVIDIA guaranteeing a series of financing instruments to improve lending conditions, given OpenAI's lack of investment-grade credit rating. Anthropic, Microsoft, and Google are also reportedly in discussions for site access. This mega-project represents a structural, multi-year demand catalyst for Taiwan's AI hardware supply chain — particularly Hon Hai — and underscores the increasingly deep interlinkage between U.S. AI ecosystems and Taiwan manufacturers. Fund managers with exposure to Hon Hai should monitor confirmation of contract details and capex timelines closely.

high.title: [Hon Hai Subsidiary Foxconn Industrial Internet (FII) Launches Share Buyback of Up to RMB 2 Billion to Defend Share Price]
high.summary:
Hon Hai (2317) announced on July 27 that its A-share listed subsidiary, Foxconn Industrial Internet (FII / 工業富聯), will conduct a share repurchase program via centralized competitive bidding, with total buyback funds ranging between RMB 1 billion and RMB 2 billion, at a price cap of RMB 103 per share, funded entirely from the company's own resources. The buyback is to be completed within three months of board approval. The trigger for this action is a cumulative 20% decline in FII's share price over 20 consecutive trading days — a threshold under Chinese securities regulations that permits defensive buybacks.

The announcement is particularly notable given FII's strong underlying fundamentals: the company pre-announced H1 2026 net profit of RMB 23.4–24.4 billion, representing year-on-year growth of 93–101%, with Q2 net profit alone of RMB 12.8–13.8 billion (up 86–101% YoY). AI server revenue from cloud service providers (CSPs) surged over 230% YoY in H1. The disconnect between strong earnings and share price weakness underscores broader A-share market volatility. For investors in Hon Hai (2317) on TWSE, this signals parent-level confidence in FII's value, reinforcing the AI server supply chain thesis. Monitor whether this stabilizes FII's A-share price, which could positively influence Hon Hai's consolidated valuation sentiment.

high.title: Taiwan Stock Market: Foreign Investors Turn Net Buyers; All Eyes on Fed FOMC Rate Decision
high.summary: Taiwan's equity market staged a remarkable intraday reversal on July 27, with the TAIEX recovering from a session low of approximately 42,949 points before closing down just 20 points at 43,634 — a V-shaped recovery of over 660 points from trough to close. The catalyst was a pivotal shift in foreign investor positioning: after being net sellers in early trading, foreign institutions turned net buyers to the tune of NT$8.04 billion, drawing in short-term retail momentum alongside. Critically, the Fed's FOMC rate decision on July 30 is keeping market participants cautious. Analysts warn that if the index fails to rally today (July 28), it risks decisively breaking below the quarterly moving average, opening the door to a retest of the July 20 low at 41,967. Among key large-caps, TSMC (2330) closed flat, while MediaTek (2454) and Delta Electronics (2308) each fell over 1.6%. Hon Hai (2317) managed to close in positive territory. The foreign investor reversal is the most important near-term signal, but the overhang of the FOMC decision means directional conviction remains limited until Wednesday.

high.title: Taiwan Stocks Stabilized by Three Major Buying Forces; Currency Market Has Three Key Focal Points This Week
high.summary: Taiwan's market on July 27 saw a dramatic intraday swing, with the TAIEX plunging 685 points to 42,969 at its worst before recovering, supported by three distinct buying forces: foreign investors, life insurers, and major proprietary accounts — all concentrated in heavyweight stocks including TSMC. This is a notable signal for life insurer watchers, as domestic insurers were active stabilizers at a critical technical level. On the currency front, the New Taiwan Dollar initially weakened before reversing to close at NT$32.305 per USD, appreciating NT$0.053 (0.16%), on NT$2.072 billion in FX turnover. Banking sources identified three key forex variables this week: (1) foreign investor net flows in Taiwan equities; (2) geopolitical risk appetite and its impact on USD demand; and (3) monetary policy signals from the U.S. Fed, Bank of England, and Bank of Japan. The consensus outlook is for the NTD to remain range-bound with a slight downside bias in the near term. Foreign buying was concentrated in UMC (2303, NT$5.28B net buy) and Nan Ya Plastics (1303, NT$3.24B net buy), rather than TSMC directly.

medium.title: Delta Electronics Reportedly Signs USD 2 Billion SiC Supply Agreement with Infineon, Signaling NVIDIA 800VDC Breakthrough
medium.summary: Market sources indicate Delta Electronics (2308) has signed a long-term supply agreement (LTA) with German power semiconductor giant Infineon for silicon carbide (SiC) components worth approximately USD 2 billion (NTD 65 billion) — its first such LTA since the COVID-19 pandemic. SiC is a critical component in NVIDIA's 800VDC AI power architecture, and the scale of this procurement commitment is being interpreted by industry observers as evidence of a key breakthrough in Delta's NVIDIA order pipeline. This matters because Delta's stock had recently corrected sharply on market rumors of delays to the 800VDC architecture rollout. Delta's President & COO Vincent Chang had previously stated 800VDC demand would surge by 2027 at the latest, and that Delta is developing solid-state transformers (SST) combining SiC and high-frequency power electronics to replace traditional silicon-based transformers. Delta's investor day is scheduled for July 30 — the same day as Apple's earnings — where the 800VDC deployment timeline will be a key focus for institutional investors.

medium.title: Taiwan Stock Market Volatility Intensifies at High Levels — Three Key Factors to Drive Direction This Week
medium.summary:
Taiwan equities experienced sharp high-level volatility last week, with the market staging a significant washout of over 1,000 points, as investor concerns around AI monetization and escalating Middle East tensions weighed on sentiment. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 4.25% on Friday, TSMC's ADR fell 2.93%, and Taiwan index futures dropped 445 points overnight to 43,369, signaling continued caution heading into this week.

Market strategists at Fubon Securities and Yongfeng Securities identified three pivotal drivers for the week ahead: (1) US mega-cap tech earnings, particularly Microsoft and Meta on July 30 and Amazon on July 31, which will serve as a critical litmus test for whether AI capex spending is translating into revenue; (2) the Federal Reserve's FOMC rate decision; and (3) developments in Middle East geopolitics. Google's latest earnings, despite strong headline numbers, showed negative free cash flow — reinforcing market anxiety over AI return on investment.

medium.title: NVIDIA Raises GPU Card Prices Again by Up to 30% — Gigabyte, Leadtek and Peers Set to Benefit
medium.summary: NVIDIA has issued its third GPU price increase of the year — following rounds in January and May — raising graphics card prices by approximately 20–30%, primarily driven by rising DRAM costs. Samsung has guided Q3 DRAM prices up 20%, which industry observers expect to ripple through to domestic memory makers Nanya Technology (2408) and Winbond (2344). Taiwan add-in board manufacturers including ASUS (2357), MSI (2377), Gigabyte (2376), and Leadtek (2465) are seen as operational beneficiaries from the price hike environment. Notably, this round expands beyond the high-end RTX 5090 series (targeted in May) to broader GeForce product lines. Retail channel distributors are reportedly hoarding inventory in anticipation of further price appreciation. While the pricing tailwind supports margins for board makers, sustained DRAM cost inflation could also compress unit economics if pass-through proves incomplete.

medium.title: Taiwan Cement (TCC) Activates European Listing Plan "Project Arcadia" — Chairman Defines Low-Carbon Building Materials Strategy
medium.summary: Taiwan Cement (1101) Chairman Chang An-ping and President Cheng Yao-hui held a video conference with an initial group of international investment banks and advisors on July 27, formally launching "Project Arcadia" — TCC's European listing initiative. The project, first disclosed at TCC's 80th anniversary event in May, aims to position the company in European capital markets as a next-generation low-carbon building materials enterprise rather than a traditional cement producer. The listing strategy and timeline will be submitted for board approval in August. For investors, a European listing could expand TCC's investor base, improve ESG-linked valuation multiples, and accelerate access to green financing, though execution risk and timeline uncertainty remain key variables to monitor.

medium.title: [Apple AI Smart Glasses Delayed — Possibly to June 2027 WWDC — Putting Pressure on Largan Precision, Genius Electronic Optical, and HTC]
medium.summary: According to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, Apple's first AI smart glasses (codenamed N50) — originally expected to launch by end-2026 — may be delayed to the June 2027 WWDC developer conference, with commercial availability pushed to late 2027. The key bottleneck is unresolved privacy concerns, which Apple's Vision hardware team has designated a top priority. This delay introduces meaningful uncertainty for Taiwan-listed optical component suppliers, including Largan Precision (玉晶光, 3406), Genius Electronic Optical (揚明光, 3504), and HTC (2498), all of which had positioned themselves as beneficiaries of Apple's smart glasses supply chain ramp. Investors in these names should reassess near-term demand assumptions and revenue timelines given this development.

medium.title: [Foxconn Industrial Internet Share Buyback — Duplicate Disclosure: RMB 1–2 Billion Competitive Bidding Repurchase]
medium.summary: This article covers the same FII buyback announcement as Article 3 above, filed as an earlier disclosure at 19:54. Key terms are identical: buyback via centralized competitive bidding, total funds RMB 1–2 billion, price cap of RMB 103/share, three-month window, self-funded. The duplication suggests this was an initial wire report followed by a fuller version — no additional material information beyond what is covered in the HIGH IMPORTANCE entry above.

medium.title: Japan BoJ Rate Hike Bets Accelerate to October; PM Takaichi's Approval Rating Slumps
medium.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae reaffirmed that monetary policy decisions rest solely with the Bank of Japan, even as markets increasingly price in an accelerated rate hike timeline. With the yen weakening to 163.99 per USD — its lowest since November 1986 — and inflation pressures compounded by oil prices near $100/barrel, market probability of a BoJ rate hike to 1.25% by October has surged to nearly 90%, up from ~60% in late June. The BoJ last raised rates to 1.0% in June, a 30-year high. For Taiwan fund managers, a more aggressive BoJ tightening cycle has direct implications: it could accelerate yen carry trade unwinding, potentially driving capital flows back into Asia including Taiwan, and may pressure Taiwan life insurers with unhedged JPY-denominated asset exposures. Takaichi's slumping approval ratings (driven by public dissatisfaction with inflation relief measures) add political uncertainty to the monetary policy outlook.

medium.title: ABF Substrate Trio Gross Margins Trending Up; Analysts Expect Unimicron Profit Growth to Continue
medium.summary: Taiwan's three leading ABF substrate makers — Unimicron (3037), Kinsus, and Nan Ya PCB — are set to report earnings, with analysts broadly optimistic. Unimicron holds a board meeting on July 28 to release financials, followed by an investor conference on July 29. June revenue hit a record NT$14.897 billion (+6% MoM, +36.3% YoY), with H1 revenue totaling NT$80.336 billion (+28.4% YoY). Analysts expect sequential profit growth and rising gross margins across all three names. Notably, Nan Ya PCB has reportedly stopped signing long-term contracts for ABF substrates, shifting to spot pricing — with Q3 pricing expected to rise by double digits QoQ, reflecting tight supply. Industry observers project the global substrate market will remain a seller's market through at least 2028, underpinned by AI demand. These companies are direct beneficiaries of TSMC-driven AI chip packaging demand, making their earnings trajectory a useful proxy for broader AI supply chain health.

medium.title: Hon Hai and Delta Electronics Among Four Attractive Stocks Tied to NVIDIA Supply Chain
medium.summary: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang reiterated that Vera Rubin chips have entered mass production, boosting outlook for Taiwan supply chain names including Hon Hai (2317) and Delta Electronics (2308). Hon Hai posted record Q2 revenues, beating market expectations. Analysts highlight Hon Hai's dominance in AI server assembly — covering both GPU and ASIC segments — and expect it to maintain 40%+ market share. High-margin in-house components are seen driving absolute profit growth. CPO switches are expected to ramp in H2, with EV models set to ship to Australia and New Zealand in H2. Q3 guidance points to double-digit QoQ and YoY growth in both AI cabinets and ICT products. Delta Electronics is passing through price increases in Q3, supported by strong AI server AC/DC and DC/DC power supply orders alongside steady conventional server demand. Both names remain key beneficiaries of the ongoing AI infrastructure buildout and warrant close monitoring ahead of Q3 earnings.

medium.title: Taiwan Dollar Closes at 32.305, Appreciating 5.3 Points
medium.summary: The New Taiwan Dollar closed at 32.305 against the US dollar on July 27, strengthening 5.3 pips (+0.16%), with total trading volume of USD 1.437 billion. The NTD opened at 32.37, touching an intraday high of 32.24 and low of 32.408 before closing at 32.305. The modest but consistent TWD appreciation trend is relevant for life insurers with large unhedged USD-denominated foreign asset portfolios, as currency gains can pressure foreign investment returns and net worth. Fund managers should monitor whether the CBC intervenes to cap further appreciation, particularly given ongoing export momentum from AI-related shipments.
